_meta.indication: PARSABIV is indicated for the treatment of secondary hyperparathyroidism (HPT) in adult patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) on hemodialysis.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter, parallel-group, 26-week study; patients randomized 1:1 to Parsabiv or placebo
pivotal_trials.population: Adults older than 18 years with CKD requiring hemodialysis three times a week for at least 3 months and a diagnosis of SHPT (mean PTH ≥ 400 pg/ml)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of subjects with a mean decrease of ≥ 30% in plasma PTH from baseline during the efficacy assessment period (weeks 20 to 27)
pivotal_trials.result: Responders (>30% PTH reduction at EAP): 188 (74%) etelcalcetide vs 21 (8%) placebo; p<0.001

nct_ctgov.title: Efficacy and Safety of Etelcalcetide (AMG 416) in the Treatment of Secondary Hyperparathyroidism (SHPT) in Patients With Chronic Kidney Disease on Hemodialysis

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter, parallel-group, 26-week study; design identical to Study 229
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with CKD on hemodialysis and a diagnosis of secondary hyperparathyroidism
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of subjects with a mean decrease of ≥ 30% in plasma PTH from baseline during the efficacy assessment period (weeks 20 to 27)
pivotal_trials.result: Responders (>30% PTH reduction at EAP): 192 (75%) etelcalcetide vs 25 (10%) placebo; p<0.001

nct_ctgov.title: Efficacy and Safety of Etelcalcetide (AMG 416) in the Treatment of Secondary Hyperparathyroidism (SHPT) in Patients With Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD) on Hemodialysis

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥5%) were blood calcium decreased (64% vs 10% placebo), muscle spasms (12% vs 7%), diarrhea (11% vs 9%), nausea (11% vs 6%), vomiting (9% vs 5%), headache (8% vs 6%), hypocalcemia (7% vs 0.2%), and paresthesia (6% vs 1%). Key warnings: hypocalcemia (sometimes severe, with QT prolongation risk), worsening heart failure, upper GI bleeding, and adynamic bone.
target_moa: Etelcalcetide is a calcimimetic (calcium-sensing receptor agonist) that allosterically modulates the CaSR on parathyroid chief cells, enhancing activation by extracellular calcium and thereby decreasing PTH secretion.

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee meeting was held because the drug is not first in class and the application did not raise significant safety or efficacy issues unexpected for the class.

summary.text: Parsabiv (etelcalcetide) received traditional (Standard-review) approval on the NDA received August 24, 2015; efficacy was established in two adequate and well-controlled placebo-controlled trials using PTH reduction as an accepted surrogate. FDA first issued a Complete Response (August 24, 2016) over the sponsor's superiority-vs-cinacalcet claim, and the drug was approved after a December 9, 2016 resubmission. No advisory committee was convened.

citations.quote:
Priority or Standard	Standard
Submit Date(s)	August 24, 2015
Received Date(s)	August 24, 2015

The applicant demonstrated, in two adequate and well-controlled trials carried out in adults with secondary hyperparathyroidism due to CKD on hemodialysis, that Parsabiv significantly reduced baseline PTH levels compared to placebo at the end of 6 months.
We acknowledge receipt of your amendment dated December 9, 2016, which constituted a complete response to our August 24, 2016, action letter.

An Advisory Committee meeting was not held as the drug is not the first in its class and the application did not raise significant safety or efficacy issues that were unexpected for this class in the intended population.

basis.text: Per the summary review, the Division issued the Complete Response because agreement between the Applicant and the Division on the proposed labeling could not be reached. The underlying clinical deficiency in the CR letter was that Study 20120360 did not provide the substantial evidence necessary to support a claim that etelcalcetide will have superior efficacy compared to cinacalcet in the treatment of secondary hyperparathyroidism in patients with CKD on hemodialysis.
